Subject: Post-call recap: TCO-focused follow-up & next steps

Hi Jordan / Priya -

Thanks for the time today - great discussion. Below is a short recap of what we heard, the levers we recommend for cost/TCO optimization, and suggested next steps. Please reply with any corrections or priorities and we'll schedule the deep technical follow-up.

What we heard (pain points)
- Rapid growth in monthly token consumption (you mentioned ~800M-1B tokens / month run rate).
- High per-token spend on peak/critical endpoints; procurement limited budget for FY26.
- Elevated P95 latency (spikes during bursts) impacting user experience.
- Minimal caching/prefix reuse today; no reserved capacity in place.

Goals / success criteria
- Reduce monthly inference spend by ~25-35% while keeping p95 latency < 150ms for critical flows.
- Predictable unit economics for procurement (a capped committed price option would be helpful).
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 + SSO needed for procurement sign-off.

Recommended levers (short list + expectations)
1) Batching + dynamic batch sizing - reduces kernel overhead for small requests; expect ~10-20% CPU/GPU efficiency gains for conversational workloads.
2) KV / prefix caching - for repeat prefixes (chat assistants, templated prompts) can cut repeated token compute by 15-30% depending on hit rate.
3) Model tiering (route non-critical traffic to smaller/quantized variants) - for embeddings or summarization flows move to a lower-cost model; expected per-token compute reduction 30-50% for those paths.
4) Quantization & compilation profiles - 8-bit/4-bit where acceptable to cut instance cost, typical additional 10-25% savings without quality regression for these use-cases.
5) Reserved dedicated capacity + burst buffer - trade committed spend for ~30-40% lower unit cost on sustained traffic.

Initial ballpark economics (very rough; we'll refine with logs)
- Baseline (your current mix) estimate: ~$42,000 / month for 1B tokens (based on the usage profile you described).
- With batching + caching + tiering: projected ~$28,000 / month (~33% savings).
- With reserved dedicated commit (12mo) + the above: projected ~$18,000 / month (~57% vs baseline).

Attachments: I've attached a short TCO worksheet (redwood-tco-worksheet.xlsx) with the assumptions above and a dedicated-pricing summary.

Next steps proposed
- Confirm which flows are "critical" (need <150ms p95) vs "best-effort" so we can map routing rules.
- Technical deep-dive (30-45m) with your infra/engineers to review call patterns and caching opportunities - Rafael (cc'd) can join.
- Procurement: we can prepare a draft MPA and committed pricing examples for your review.

Suggested slots: Thu 2/19 10:00-11:00am PT or Fri 2/20 9:00-10:00am PT - let me know what works.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
